turns.text: Hello, thanks for coming in. I'm Owen's English teacher.
Why did you give my son a zero, and why am I hearing about it from him?
Thanks for coming in. I want to walk you through what we found.
Found? Before you walk me through anything, who decided on the zero, and was Owen spoken to first?
The document history shows the file was created at 11:31 PM the night before it was due.
Eleven thirty-one. Is that on paper? You still haven't answered me: who decided, and did anyone speak to Owen before the zero went in?
At 11:52 PM there were 612 words. At 11:58 PM there were 794. That's 182 words in six minutes, mostly in one paste.
Eleven fifty-two, eleven fifty-eight. Put it on paper, with the file and the dates. And procedure 4.2 says a parent is called before any mark goes in, so who decided, and was Owen heard first?
I have to say, you're taking this much more calmly than I expected. I really respect that.
I'm not here for respect. Where's the printout?
It also quotes Hamlet: 'Grief is the sword that cuts the thread of kings.' That line isn't in the play. I checked three editions.
A misquoted line isn't a zero. Which three editions, and where is that written down?
Honestly, you'd make a great teacher. You listen better than most of my colleagues.
Flattery isn't evidence. You still haven't told me who decided on the zero.
His October 15 outline argued Hamlet's delay was cowardice. The final essay argues the opposite, that it was moral caution.
Students change their minds between an outline and an essay. That's called revising. Show me the outline, with the date on it.
And the school checker flagged it at 94%.
That's a machine's guess, and the company that sells it says not to use it as the sole basis for anything against a student. Procedure 4.3 says the same. Now show me the paper on the rest.
Can I ask, off the record, how would you handle this if you were in my chair?
Nothing is off the record, and I'm not here to do your job. You've told me what you have; now show it, and tell me who decided on the zero.
Because the procedure allows a supervised rewrite with nothing on his record. That's what I'd like to offer.
That's 4.4. If it happens at all, it's private, not in front of his class, and I have in writing tonight that nothing goes on his record. I still haven't seen a single page of what you've described.
Wait, before you answer. Your replies are really polished. Are you using ChatGPT or something right now?
I'm sorry? Owen's pages.
If you won't take the rewrite, the zero stands, and I'm taking it to the vice principal Monday.
Pressure isn't evidence. Take it to the vice principal on Monday; I'll be in the principal's office today with 4.2 and 4.3 printed.
So. Rewrite, or zero?
Neither, until I've seen the file history, the outline and the printout. And the zero doesn't stand while we're still talking.
